svg.title: Why the average dot product cannot measure uniformity but the Gaussian potential can
svg.desc: Six point configurations on the circle are shown as rings of dots: uniform, eight equispaced, four equispaced, two antipodal, two clusters, and a concentrated von Mises-Fisher sample. The average pairwise dot product is essentially zero for the first four, including the two antipodal points that are maximally non-uniform, so it cannot distinguish them. The log average Gaussian potential separates all six in the expected order.
svg.text: The same six configurations, scored two ways
all ≈ 0, so it cannot tell them apart
